findings.desc: Closeout receipt replay does not prove the current write was canonical. latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepts any historical receipt whose artifactDigest matches current bytes and whose headHash is merely an ancestor; it does not bind the receipt to the commit/change under review or require the receipt to be newly minted with that artifact change. Reverting an artifact manually to previously receipted bytes therefore reuses the old canonical writer claim and passes retention. More generally receiptHash is recomputable from a public salt, so a manual writer can self-assert a canonical writerCommand. This violates CHK-004/CHK-005 manual, replayed, and stale-provenance fail-closed guarantees.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565: v2 per-artifact integrity chain requires the latest receipt, intact sequence/previous hash, receipt introduction commit equal to latest artifact-changing commit, and receipt pre-write head equal to that commit parent. Exact A to B to manual A replay, copy, and reorder regressions pass. npm test and closeout smoke pass.

findings.desc: The delivery-context runtime validator accepts semantically invalid payloads that CHK-003 says must fail closed. validatePersistedDeliveryContextPack leaves candidateRouting and validation completely unchecked, does not exact-key or type-check claims, accepts non-string entries in diff.changedFiles/testFiles/evidenceCommands, and does not validate deliveryCheck.ref. A structurally plausible pack such as changedFiles:[42] with arbitrary candidateRouting/validation and extra claims fields is treated as trusted, while the smoke only tests authorityDone=true. Tighten the persisted schema to the producer contract and add adversarial cases.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565: delivery context now exact-validates claims, string arrays, candidate routing, validation evidence, review round, delivery ref, and waiver nested shapes. Adversarial malformed nested payload regressions pass.

findings.desc: Receipt replay defeats the claimed manual/stale-write rejection. latestValidCloseoutReceipt filters all historical receipts for the path and returns any matching valid record, so after canonical A then canonical B, a manual revert of the artifact to A is accepted under the old receipt even though the latest write was not canonical. Reproduced against dist: receipts [A@2026-01-01,B@2026-01-02] plus current summary.json=A returned acceptedTimestamp=2026-01-01. Bind receipts to the actual write/commit and reject superseded/replayed receipts (including copied/reordered receipt-ledger entries).
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. Only the final intact receipt-chain entry can qualify, and its introduction commit must equal the latest artifact-changing commit with pre-write HEAD as parent. A-to-B-to-manual-A replay, copy, and reorder regressions pass.

findings.desc: The 15-intent evidence overstates CLI/integration coverage. CHK-004 is type=cli and requires canonical parent_ledger_rollup_set output, but closeout-trust-smoke never invokes that handler/CLI; it calls store.writeProofStoryParentLedgerRollup plus autoCommitStoryMetadata directly. Likewise none of the newly wired validate, done_required_validate, delivery_check_set/waiver, evaluate_save, summary_set, delivery_context_pack, or live_smoke_transcript handler paths are executed. The smoke can stay green if a handler omits or passes the wrong closeoutArtifactPaths. Add at least one real CLI/handler regression for parent_ledger_rollup_set and table-driven integration coverage for every registered canonical writer path; wire this high-risk smoke into routine test discovery/evidence.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. The closeout smoke executes all supported canonical writer-path pairs through real handlers, including parent rollup and legacy test writers, and routine npm test includes test:closeout-trust. Full npm test exits 0.

findings.desc: Trusted artifact runtime schemas accept missing required timestamps and semantically invalid delivery-context fields. Repro after the story build: calling validateTrustedMilestoneLedger with createdAt removed, validateTrustedSlicePlan with updatedAt removed, and validateTrustedParentLedgerRollup with createdAt removed all return successfully; validatePersistedDeliveryContextPack also accepts changedFiles:[42], testFiles:[42], evidenceCommands:[{}], and deliveryCheck.ref as a string. This contradicts CHK-003 edge/adversarial and means malformed persisted payloads can cross the new trust boundary. Require/validate createdAt+updatedAt (including ISO shape), validate optional typed fields/semantic relationships, require string arrays for delivery paths/commands, validate ref null/object and exact claims shape, and add negative regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. Ledger, plan, and rollup require ISO createdAt and updatedAt plus strict nested fields; delivery pack nested schema is exact. Missing timestamp and malformed payload regressions pass.

findings.desc: The closed writer-provenance table names writers that cannot produce the receipts required by the real retention gate. test-evidence.json lists test_add/test_story, but those handlers write the artifact without autoCommitStoryMetadata(closeoutArtifactPaths), so their declared canonical output is always rejected as missing/stale receipt. More critically, evidence/transcript-diff.md is assigned to live_smoke_transcript, but that command only writes evidence/live-smoke-transcript.json; the TEST lifecycle hint still instructs users to hand-write transcript-diff.md. Following that normal closeout instruction therefore invalidates review retention, and the verifier only checks that writer command names exist, not that they attest the listed path. Align the closed policy with real writer choke points (or add explicit CLI writers/receipts), preserve intentional legacy compatibility, and add an end-to-end regression for every declared path/writer pair.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 812a711565. test_add and test_story now attest test evidence; test_story commits after final metadata write; phantom transcript-diff policy is removed; TEST UX directs canonical live smoke JSON with an explicit capture command. Every policy writer pair runs in smoke.

findings.desc: The v2 chain closes historical replay/copy/reorder, but still does not prove the current write came from a canonical handler. Every receipt field and integrityHash is publicly computable. Reproduced in a fresh git repo without calling summary_set or autoCommitStoryMetadata: manually write summary.json plus a sequence=1 receipt claiming writerCommand=summary_set, set headHash/materialHash/storyFilesHash to the parent, commit both together, and latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepts it (accepted=true, writer=summary_set). This violates CHK-001 canonical writer provenance and CHK-004 adversarial manual/wrong-writer rejection. Add an authority boundary the manual writer cannot mint (or narrow the claim/threat model and intents); include this exact counterfeit-current-receipt negative in the smoke.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 065b7dde13: closeout receipts are now signed by a per-story/per-review-round Ed25519 key whose public identity is bound into the exact ReviewRun; manual co-commit forgery, wrong-key signing, signer rotation replay, and old-key replay are rejected by regression coverage.

findings.desc: F-001 was only partially resolved: the v2 chain prevents historical receipt replay, but it still does not distinguish a canonical CLI write from a hand-crafted co-commit. Repro against current dist created summary.json manually, built a v2 receipt with writerCommand=summary_set using the exported deterministic builder, committed artifact+receipt together with an arbitrary manual commit, and latestValidCloseoutReceipt returned ACCEPTED forged writer=summary_set. The causal checks all pass because artifactCommit equals receipt introductionCommit and receipt.headHash is its parent. Reclassifying the receipt as non-signed is honest, but CHK-001 canonical writer provenance and CHK-004/CHK-005 manual-write fail-closed guarantees still require a mechanically trusted writer fact. Bind provenance to an existing non-forgeable/controlled command event or signed CLI artifact, or narrow the acceptance claim; add this exact forged co-commit regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 065b7dde13: the causal receipt no longer trusts a self-reported public key; verification is anchored to the signer identity embedded in the exact signed ReviewRun and rejects independently minted co-commit receipts.

findings.desc: Canonical closeout receipt/auto-commit is broken for a valid wrapper-root layout where metadataRoot differs from gitRoot and storyDir is configured inside gitRoot (for example gitRoot=repo, storyDir=repo/.lattice/story/actives). autoCommitStoryMetadata resolves gitCwd to <wrapper>/repo but constructs storyRel directly from the metadata-root-relative config and probes <gitCwd>/repo/.lattice/...; the actual story is <gitCwd>/.lattice/.... In a real temp Git reproduction evaluateStoryDirInsideGitRoot returned ok:true with rel=.lattice/story/actives/B-wrap, while autoCommitStoryMetadata returned an empty hint and git status retained ?? .lattice/. Thus canonical closeout writers silently produce neither commit nor receipt and later retention/clean-tree gates fail. Derive the staged/provenance path by relativizing the canonical StoryStore storyDirPath against resolved gitCwd (and fail closed if outside), and add wrapper-root receipt coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 065b7dde13: wrapper-root story-relative paths now use canonical realpath containment relative to the git root, preventing doubled prefixes; the real wrapper-root autoCommit and receipt regression passes.

findings.desc: The Ed25519 repair still does not establish the claimed exact ReviewRun-bound canonical writer provenance. The private key is stored as plaintext mode-0600 under project-accessible .lattice/runtime and is returned by the exported loadReviewRoundReceiptSigner/loadOrCreateReviewRoundReceiptSigner API, so the same local actor that can hand-write story metadata can read the trusted key and sign a forged co-commit. Repro against current dist: load the round signer, manually write summary.json, build a receipt claiming writerCommand=summary_set, sign it with signer.privateKey, append and commit both; latestValidCloseoutReceipt returns `ACCEPTED exact-key manual forge`. The current smoke tests only an attacker-generated wrong key. Also the signer path hashes only reviewRound, and repeated loadOrCreate calls in one round return the same key (`sameRoundKeyReused true`), so it is round-scoped rather than exact-ReviewRun scoped as claimed. Keep the signing capability outside the manual writer threat domain and bind/authorize it per exact reviewRunId (or narrow the contract honestly); add correct-key exfiltration and same-round distinct-run regressions.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by c7fc14674c and f10e43b8ee: removed persistent review-round signer authority and narrowed local receipts to audit-only causal telemetry. latestValidCloseoutReceipt now deliberately rejects all same-UID local receipts; the real consumer proves an exact coherent manual forge remains inadmissible and a fresh post-closeout review succeeds.

findings.desc: Wrapper-root metadata retention still uses the metadata-root-relative configured storyDir as though it were git-root-relative. In evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention, projectRoot is the resolved git root and changedFilesBetween returns .lattice/story/actives/B-wrap/..., but storyPrefix is built from store.storyDirRel() as repo/.lattice/story/actives/B-wrap/. The filter therefore sees no changed story artifacts. A real split-root fixture with gitRoot=repo and storyDir=repo/.lattice/story/actives committed unknown-manual.json after the review snapshot; git diff reported .lattice/story/actives/B-wrap/unknown-manual.json while evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention returned {ok:true,reasons:[]}. Rebase the canonical StoryStore story directory relative to projectRoot exactly as autoCommit now does, reject outside paths, and cover unknown/manual plus canonical receipt cases through the real retention consumer in wrapper-root mode.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by c7fc14674c: metadata-only retention now derives story paths canonically relative to gitRoot under wrapper-root configurations. The real wrapper fixture commits unknown-manual.json and the retention consumer rejects it with the named path; scope/process contracts pass.

findings.desc: The new Ed25519 key does not authenticate that a write came from a canonical command against the stated same-workspace manual-writer adversary. The private key is a predictable local runtime file readable by the same OS user that can hand-edit story metadata, and loadReviewRoundReceiptSigner plus signCloseoutWriteReceipt are directly usable by that process. In a real wrapper fixture I loaded the exact review-round private key, manually wrote summary.json, built a receipt claiming writerCommand=summary_set with the current HEAD/hashes, appended it, and committed both; latestValidCloseoutReceipt accepted it. The regression only uses an independently generated attacker key, so it misses this capability-reuse attack. Mode 0600 separates OS users but cannot distinguish the canonical CLI from manual code running as the project user (and load does not reject a key file whose mode has become permissive). Either use a signer capability isolated from arbitrary project-user reads, or narrow the claim/threat model; add a same-key manual co-commit regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by c7fc14674c and f10e43b8ee: mode-0600 same-UID key storage was removed from the authority model and runtime registry. Local receipts are explicitly audit-only; exact same-UID artifact plus coherent receipt forgery is accepted only as causal telemetry and rejected by gate-authoritative lookup, requiring fresh review.

findings.desc: The implementation correctly makes local causal receipts audit-only, but the process-fact registry still falsely classifies closeout-write-receipts.jsonl as gate evidence. The entry retains semantics=[artifact,schema-contract,freshness-policy,gate-evidence] and consumerGate=REVIEW evidence metadata-only retention gate, while REVIEW_RETENTION_PROTOCOL_METADATA_PATHS explicitly ignores the receipt file, latestValidCloseoutReceipt returns null without reading it, and latestCausallyValidCloseoutReceipt has no production consumer. This contradicts the registry rationale (not authority/not closeout evidence) and the project rule that gate-consumed facts must match actual mechanical consumers. Reclassify the artifact as audit/telemetry with no gate-evidence semantic or claimed consumer; keep the fail-closed authoritative boundary as the L4 runtime gate fact.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 79f4a84f01: closeout-write-receipts.jsonl is registered as unsigned L1 audit-only artifact with no consumerGate; the separate L4 runtime closeout trust boundary remains the mechanical DONE gate fact, and the process contract pins both classifications.

findings.desc: Revised receipt semantics are honest at the helper boundary, but the promised fresh-review requirement is not mechanically enforced on the actual TEST→DONE path. evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention/collectReviewerEvidenceState reject a pre-closeout review after closeout metadata changes, yet canFinishGuard never consumes either function; reviewer evidence is checked only on REVIEW→TEST. Therefore a TEST-phase closeout writer can change summary/test/delivery metadata and still reach DONE through the remaining DONE gates without a fresh reviewer pass. The smoke test only constructs a synthetic fresh RR-002 and calls the helper directly while the story is in TEST, so it does not prove lifecycle enforcement. Add TEST/DONE gate consumption plus an end-to-end transition regression, while accounting for legitimate REVIEW→TEST phase/index mutations so the new gate does not self-invalidate every pass.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 79f4a84f01: actual canFinishGuard and DONE failure reason consume closeout-aware reviewer evidence freshness. A real XState TEST FINISH regression proves post-review closeout change remains TEST with stale_closeout_review, then a fresh post-closeout run/pass reaches DONE while protocol phase/index metadata is tolerated.

findings.desc: F-014 is not fixed for the real persisted lifecycle: a normal REVIEW→TEST update to index.json invalidates every REVIEW run before DONE. evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention treats index.json as an unknown closeout artifact because it is not in the protocol allowlist and has no narrow phase-transition exception. A real Git fixture captured a REVIEW snapshot, changed only StoryInfo.phase from REVIEW to TEST, committed the normal index.json metadata, and then returned ok:false with `untrusted closeout artifact path: index.json` and `invalid closeout artifact: index.json`. The added smoke starts with phase TEST and drives only the in-memory XState FINISH event, so it never exercises story_advance persistence. Add a narrowly validated REVIEW→TEST index transition allowance (currentReviewRound and non-transition story semantics unchanged), not a blanket index.json ignore, and test via actual persisted transition before TEST→DONE guard/reason parity.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0bc3da31f3: added a narrow persisted REVIEW-to-TEST index transition validator that compares the signed review HEAD index to current TEST index, permits only exact phase/event/provenance deltas, and rejects title or stable-field tampering. Real committed git regression passes.

findings.desc: F-014 fix wires closeout-aware reviewer freshness into the real TEST→DONE canFinishGuard and emits stale_closeout_review, but the recovery path deadlocks on the legitimate REVIEW→TEST lifecycle mutation. A review run/pass is necessarily captured in REVIEW; story_advance TEST then persists phase=TEST and events into index.json after that snapshot. index.json is not in REVIEW_RETENTION_PROTOCOL_METADATA_PATHS, so evaluateReviewRunMetadataRetention treats it as a changed unknown/untrusted artifact and invalidates the fresh REVIEW evidence at DONE. review_run_start/review_pass_set are allowed only in REVIEW, so TEST cannot create the post-transition snapshot needed to recover. The new smoke misses this because it initializes the persisted story directly in TEST and only exercises an in-memory FINISH actor; its synthetic fresh run is created after all metadata changes without executing the real REVIEW→TEST persistence step. Add a real lifecycle regression covering REVIEW run/pass → persisted story_advance TEST/index mutation → TEST→DONE, and classify/bind legitimate lifecycle index mutations so they do not authorize arbitrary closeout changes or deadlock DONE. Same-UID receipts remain correctly non-authoritative.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 0bc3da31f3: canonical persisted REVIEW-to-TEST index mutation is admitted only after exact signed-snapshot delta validation; normal flow no longer deadlocks, while extra title/stable/event/round/provenance mutation remains a closeout-review blocker. Production-source and contract assertions cover it.

findings.desc: The REVIEW→TEST index exception removes the deadlock and correctly rejects stable-field/round/phase/action/branch/extra-key drift, but it does not authenticate or even compare most transition provenance. evaluatePersistedReviewToTestIndexTransition accepts any non-empty event.user, event.sessionId, and event.agent, and any parseable timestamp at or after run.startedAt. Therefore changing a canonical collectContext event from the real user/session/agent/timestamp to attacker-chosen non-empty values still returns ok:true; a same-UID writer can manually forge an index delta with the accepted shape and have it treated as the canonical story_advance transition. The smoke only mutates title and has no negative cases for user/sessionId/agent/timestamp, despite the contract requiring provenance mutation to block. Bind the exception to mechanically verifiable transition provenance (or a gate-authoritative transition artifact) and add negative tests for each provenance field; shape/presence alone cannot distinguish production collectContext from a same-UID manual write. Post-closeout artifacts remain correctly blocking and same-UID receipts remain non-authoritative.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 33c15f851f: local event identity/timestamp/branch strings are explicitly audit-only and authorization-neutral. DONE independently reruns the full REVIEW-to-TEST preflight over signed current review run/pass/round and gate facts, so forged provenance grants no privilege; mutations are regression-tested.

findings.desc: The exact index-transition validator also creates a false deadlock for a legitimate collectContext event when Git identity is supplied through environment rather than git config. StoryEvent.user is optional and collectContext sets it only when `git config user.name` succeeds, but evaluatePersistedReviewToTestIndexTransition requires event.user to be non-empty. In a real repo with commits authorized by GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/GIT_COMMITTER_NAME and no configured user.name, the persisted REVIEW→TEST event correctly omitted user and the validator rejected it as incomplete provenance. This is distinct from F-017’s overbroad acceptance of attacker-chosen non-empty provenance: the fix needs mechanically authoritative provenance while preserving collectContext’s documented optional user behavior, or collectContext/commit identity must be made consistently required at the producer boundary. Add the environment-identity/no-user regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 33c15f851f: transition audit identity fields are optional and non-authoritative; a repository without git user.name using environment commit identity now passes the real persisted flow. Malformed field types still fail, and DONE authorization comes from rechecked signed review/gate facts.

findings.desc: Audit provenance is now honestly authorization-neutral, but the claimed independent DONE recheck still does not replay the authoritative REVIEW→TEST reviewer gate. runReviewToTestPreflightGate checks review loops, ProofStory completeness, and CLI channel/concept/lint/docs gates; it does not invoke canPassReviewGuard or an equivalent shared evaluator for required reviewer presence, active-reviewer coverage/quorum, and open blocking findings. canFinishGuard only rejects reviewerEvidence.invalid and does not require any valid reviewer evidence or reject valid open high/critical findings. Consequently a same-UID manual REVIEW→TEST index/phase edit with the accepted stable delta can still skip the XState REVIEW_PASS guard: with no reviewer records invalid is empty, and even a signature-valid open blocking finding is not rejected at DONE, provided the unrelated DONE/preflight gates pass. The process-contract regex only proves that runReviewToTestPreflightGate is called, not that the missing signed reviewer facts are consumed. Add a shared authoritative REVIEW verdict evaluator (or explicitly re-run canPassReviewGuard semantics) at DONE and regress manual phase edits with missing reviewer evidence, missing opt-in lane/quorum, and an open blocking finding. The revised audit-only provenance and post-closeout freshness semantics themselves are sound.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 1baeb54a9d: extracted shared phase-agnostic evaluateReviewVerdict consumed by REVIEW-to-TEST and TEST-to-DONE boolean/reason paths. It enforces current reviewer presence/binding, opt-in lanes, quorum, review loops, and open blocking findings; real DONE regressions cover no reviewer, missing lane, open high, and valid passes.

findings.desc: Shared DONE reviewer verdict is bypassable when currentReviewRound is missing: collectReviewerEvidenceState calls validateEvidenceRunBinding, which returns success immediately at review-run.ts:921 before checking evidence signature, reviewRunId, run signature/workspace binding, round, or freshness. A same-UID editor can set phase=TEST, remove currentReviewRound, and add one forged lattice-review-* pass per opt-in lane; evaluateReviewVerdict then sees valid lane/quorum evidence and can authorize DONE. The new wrapper-root DONE fixture unintentionally exercises the missing-round branch (its doneStory at review-escalation-freshness-root-smoke.ts:661-673 has no currentReviewRound) but only seeds valid signed passes, so it does not detect the bypass. Missing currentReviewRound must fail closed for reviewer-required REVIEW/TEST/DONE stories, and an adversarial smoke should use tampered/missing run bindings and prove both evaluateReviewVerdict and FINISH reject them.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 709f4e5e00: reviewer-required lifecycle verdict now fails closed with review_round_missing before legacy evidence compatibility when currentReviewRound is absent. Missing round plus unsigned/tampered/missing-run passes all block real TEST FINISH; valid signed current passes still succeed.

findings.desc: DONE reviewer verdict fails open when a TEST story lacks currentReviewRound, and the updated wrapper-root fixture does not exercise signed reviewer validation. The DONE fixture creates doneStory without currentReviewRound, while validateEvidenceRunBinding returns null immediately when currentReviewRound is absent; collectReviewerEvidenceState then classifies lattice-review-* passes as valid without checking evidence signature, reviewRunId, run signature, lane, round, workspace binding, or freshness. A same-UID edit can therefore set phase=TEST, omit currentReviewRound, and insert pass-shaped reviewer records for opt-in lanes to satisfy evaluateReviewVerdict. Set currentReviewRound on the actual doneStory fixture and make missing currentReviewRound fail closed for reviewer-required REVIEW/TEST/DONE stories, with an unsigned/tampered-pass regression.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 709f4e5e00: wrapper-root DONE fixture now sets currentReviewRound and truly exercises signed pass/run binding. Added adversarial missing-round, unsigned/tampered pass, missing reviewRunId, and unknown run regressions; all fail closed with guard/reason parity.

findings.desc: The shared delivery-claim schema creates a retired-vocabulary guard bypass instead of an explicit narrow compatibility quarantine. baseline-contracts.ts is excluded wholesale by legacyQuarantineFiles, while active closeout-trust.ts imports LOCAL_ONLY_DELIVERY_CLAIM_KEYS/CLAIMS (symbol names that contain none of the banned tokens) and consumes the hidden authorityDone/fullAuthorityDone/productionDone keys. The source scanner only regex-scans each active line and does not restrict imports of these exported constants, so any future active renderer/producer can spread LOCAL_ONLY_DELIVERY_CLAIMS and emit all retired fields while the guard still passes. This contradicts the retirement contract requirement that whitelisted legacy files be explicit and narrow. Keep the exact schema/validator in a narrowly named compatibility module or explicit structural quarantine, and make the vocabulary guard enforce an allowlisted importer/usage set (including a positive control for indirect constant spreading). The current exact false-value validator and producer copies are otherwise fail-closed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 398ed6e6b5: retired delivery claims moved to a single-purpose compatibility module exposing only constructor and exact validator. Vocabulary guard enforces exact approved importers/symbols/call counts, forbids constructor spread/reexport, and positive-controls unapproved indirect import/call/spread plus direct tokens.

findings.desc: F-022 remains bypassable through a local re-export from an approved importer. scanLegacyDeliveryCompatibilityUsage only detects module specifiers resolving directly to legacy-delivery-claims-compat.ts, verifies named imports/call counts/direct-use regexes, and forbids direct constructor spreading. In approved delivery-context-pack.ts, adding `export { createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims };` changes none of those invariants (mechanical probe: compatImports=1, constructorCalls=2, directUses=2, spreadForbidden=false), so the guard passes. An unapproved module can then import the constructor from delivery-context-pack.ts and call/spread it; its specifier no longer resolves to the compatibility module, so it is not scanned. The positive control covers only a direct unapproved import and therefore misses this route. Approved importers must be forbidden from exporting/re-exporting/aliasing the compatibility symbols (including local export lists), and positive controls must cover local re-export followed by a transitive unapproved import, namespace/dynamic/direct re-export variants, and indirect constructor calls.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d9f301399f: guard blocks compat symbol export/default/property/spread/alias escapes, namespace/dynamic/require/direct reexports, and graph-scans true two-hop imports through approved importers. Positive-control matrix proves each bypass is caught.

findings.desc: The dedicated compatibility module preserves the exact all-false schema, but the new importer/usage guard does not enforce the claimed indirect boundary. scanLegacyDeliveryCompatibilityUsage only follows imports whose specifier resolves directly to legacy-delivery-claims-compat.ts. An approved importer can re-export its already-imported constructor without changing its expected import symbols, constructor call count, or direct-use count (for example export { createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims }; in delivery-context-pack.ts). An unapproved module can then import that symbol from delivery-context-pack.ts and call or spread it; it contains neither a direct compat-module import nor retired field tokens, so both the compatibility scan and vocabulary scan accept it. The positive control labeled as unapproved/indirect is actually a direct import from ./legacy-delivery-claims-compat.js and therefore does not exercise this bypass. Add explicit rejection of exports/aliases of compatibility symbols from approved importers and a true two-hop positive control (approved importer re-export or alias → unapproved consumer). Build, current guard, closeout smoke, and process contract pass, but they do not cover this transitive leak. Exact validator/producer schema semantics themselves remain correct.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by d9f301399f: approved importers cannot re-export or alias compatibility constructors; scanner follows dependency graph for transitive leakage. True two-hop positive control patches approved importer then imports from it in unapproved consumer and is rejected.

findings.desc: F-023/F-024 remain bypassable because the graph is built from regex-extracted quoted specifiers and raw identifier text rather than parsed module bindings. A static unapproved dynamic import whose exact module path is written as a JavaScript template literal is valid Node/TypeScript, but extractImportSpecifiers accepts only single/double-quoted import arguments. Both usage and graph scanners therefore see zero edges, and the caller can invoke or spread the constructor; the mechanical probe returned extracted=[]. Separately, an approved importer can export a wrapper calling the constructor through a Unicode-escaped final identifier character. JavaScript resolves it to the imported binding while the guard retains occurrence=3, call=2, direct-use=2 and no direct-export match, so no exporter edge is created. Positive controls cover only unescaped identifiers and single-quoted dynamic imports. Use an AST to resolve imports/exports and identifier bindings (including template-literal dynamic imports), or conservatively reject nonstandard dynamic loading; add positive controls for the template-literal import and escaped-identifier wrapper followed by an unapproved consumer.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by 932387b7a9: retired compatibility scanning now parses TypeScript AST bindings and module edges, recognizes exact no-substitution template-literal import(), decodes Unicode-escaped identifiers, and propagates taint across the module graph. Executable positive controls reject both reported attacks plus neighboring namespace, alias, require, quoted dynamic import, and direct re-export variants. Independent build, retired vocabulary guard, process-fact contract, closeout smoke, and implementer full npm test passed.

findings.desc: F-025’s two reported spellings are fixed, but the approved-importer containment still has an executable AST/regex metric-preservation bypass. In an isolated checkout, replace one approved `claims: createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims()` site in delivery-context-pack.ts with `claims: emitLegacyClaims()`, add `export function emitLegacyClaims() { return createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims(); }`, and add a comment (or inert string) containing `claims: createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims()`. TypeScript AST totals remain exactly identifier=3 and direct calls=2; the raw directUsePattern count remains 2 because it counts comments. Consequently usageDrift is false, directlyExportsCompatibilityBinding returns early without inspecting the exported wrapper, no exporter edge is propagated, and the complete retired-authority-vocabulary-guard-smoke exits PASS after a successful build. This exposes a reusable exported wrapper while satisfying the claimed closed importer/usage surface. Make approved usage checks entirely AST/binding based (including exact parent/call-site validation), and inspect exports regardless of metric drift; add this metric-preserving wrapper plus comment/string padding as a positive control.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by eaad32b53c: approved compatibility use is now validated by exact TypeScript AST binding references and allowed call-site parents/arguments; comments and strings cannot satisfy counts; exports/aliases/wrappers are inspected unconditionally and taint propagates regardless of local metric state. Executable padded wrapper/downstream controls pass.

findings.desc: The AST module-reference extractor remains fail-open for executable dynamic loaders. `staticModuleText` accepts only string/no-substitution-template literals and call handling requires exactly one argument (lines 335-347), so an unapproved source can load the retired compatibility module with `await import("./legacy-delivery-" + "claims-compat.js")`, an interpolated template, or a two-argument dynamic import without producing any ModuleReference; usage and graph scans then see zero compatibility imports. The new positive matrix covers only a no-substitution template literal. Conservatively reject unresolved import()/require() module expressions in active source, and accept dynamic-import option arguments while scanning argument 0; add computed/interpolated and two-argument positive controls.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by eaad32b53c: all dynamic import and require arg0 forms are inspected, static expressions are folded, and suspicious unresolved compatibility expressions fail closed; executable computed, interpolated, two-argument import, and require controls pass without rejecting unrelated plugin imports.

findings.desc: F-027 remains bypassable because unresolved loaders are filtered by the spelling of arg0 instead of resolved values/bindings. `const p = "./legacy-delivery-claims-compat.js"; const mod = await import(p, {});` has staticModuleText(p)=undefined, but scanConcealedCompatibilityLoads sees expression text only `p`, so its keyword heuristic returns no violation; the AST probe confirmed concealedViolations=[]. Loader aliases are another zero-edge path: valid CJS `const rq = require; rq("./legacy-delivery-claims-compat.js")`, `module.require(...)`, and ESM createRequire aliases are ignored because lines 356-359/458-462 recognize only a CallExpression whose callee is the literal identifier `require`. Conversely, an unrelated `import(compatPluginPath)` false-positives. The resolved claim that all dynamic import/require arg0 forms are inspected is therefore not met. Fail closed for unresolved import() in active source or implement bounded constant propagation, and bind/forbid require aliases/member/createRequire forms; add variable-indirection and alias controls plus a non-compat variable named compat false-positive control.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by aa86b4d950: TypeChecker-backed dataflow resolves const module paths and require/module.require/createRequire aliases to real declarations; loader references are no longer keyword guesses. Variable-indirect compat loads reject while shadowed and unrelated plugin identifiers remain valid.

findings.desc: The new AST call-site allowlist validates only a local syntactic shape, not the intended call sites, so an approved importer can still export compatibility-derived values without a disallowed identifier reference. In delivery-context-pack.ts, replace one sanctioned `claims: createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims()` initializer with `claims: leaked.claims`, then add `export const leaked = { claims: createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims() };`. The in-memory AST probe preserves the exact expected constructor totals (identifier occurrences=3, direct calls=2) and reports disallowedReferences=[]: matchesApprovedCallSite accepts any zero-arg call used as any object property named `claims` (lines 406-412). Because the exported call is classified approved, directlyExportsCompatibilityBinding also sees no taint; a downstream module can import `leaked` and destructure/read `.claims` with no compatibility edge. Bind approved calls to their actual enclosing function/object construction context or explicit source call-site identities, and independently reject compatibility calls inside exported statements even when their immediate parent shape is otherwise allowed. Add relocation-to-exported-claims-object plus downstream destructuring/property controls.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by aa86b4d950: exact import binding identity and full enclosing function/export ancestry replace immediate shape checks; constructor results flowing through exported local variables or functions taint the module and downstream property/destructuring consumers are rejected.

findings.desc: The F-026 resolution overstates exact binding/call-site and unconditional export containment. `isApprovedValueUse` matches identifiers by text and only checks the immediate syntactic parent (`claims` PropertyAssignment or negated if); it does not resolve the identifier to the compatibility import binding, bind the call to its canonical source location/enclosing function, or reject an otherwise approved-shaped call nested inside an exported statement. `directlyExportsCompatibilityBinding` then derives exporters only from `disallowedCompatibilityValueReferences`, so a compatibility reference that satisfies the local parent shape is omitted even when its top-level ancestor is exported. The new padded-wrapper controls move a constructor call directly under `return`, which is disallowed, but do not cover relocation into an approved-shaped `claims` property under an exported wrapper, nor lexical shadowing of the imported name. This does not meet the recorded claim of exact TypeScript AST binding references / exact call sites / unconditional wrapper inspection. Use TypeScript symbol binding (or capture the imported local declaration and compare resolved references), bind approved calls to stable canonical AST ancestry/source anchors, and inspect every exported statement for compatibility-tainted bindings independently of whether the local use shape is approved.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed by aa86b4d950 with TypeChecker symbol identity, canonical full call-site anchors, and unconditional export reachability. Same-name shadow controls remain clean and exported approved-shaped wrapper/object relocation controls reject.

findings.desc: The new call anchors and export taint still miss assignment/property-write flows, so F-029/F-030 containment is bypassable without changing binding counts or approved anchors. In delivery-context-pack.ts, add `export const leakBox: any = {};` and replace the approved nested-function initializer with `claims: (leakBox.payload = { claims: createLegacyLocalOnlyDeliveryClaims() }, leakBox.payload.claims)`. The compatibility call remains a zero-arg `claims` PropertyAssignment under the exact approved anchor `function:createDeliveryContextPackHandlers>function:deliveryContextPack`; the AST probe reports bindingReferenceCount=3, the exact two expected call anchors, and disallowed=[]. `directlyExportsCompatibilityBinding` only propagates through VariableDeclaration/FunctionDeclaration bodies (lines 805-840); leakBox’s exported declaration initializer is `{}`, while the tainted value arrives through a later BinaryExpression assignment, so leakBox is never marked tainted and downstream property/destructuring consumers have no graph edge. Track assignment/property-write flows (including exported mutable/container symbols) or forbid any compatibility call whose result is not the exact canonical return-object node, and add same-anchor exported-container mutation controls.
